needs_verification.consequence: Startup aborts with an uncaught pydantic.ValidationError traceback, and the daemon crash-loops in Docker until the user hand-edits the TOML
needs_verification.trigger: triggarr.toml containing a disabled instance such as [radarr.Old] url = "192.168.1.10:7878" enabled = false, which loaded fine before this diff

findings.problem: validate_url_ssrf now runs on every InstanceConfig.url at load time, including disabled instances. It rejects values the old model accepted, for example a URL with no scheme such as `192.168.1.10:7878` or `radarr:7878`. urlparse reads these as scheme '192.168.1.10' or 'radarr', so the check returns 'URL scheme must be http or https'. It also rejects ftp:// URLs and link-local IPs. The startup path is ensure_config -> load_settings -> Settings(**data) (triggarr/config.py:227). Its docstring (triggarr/config.py:345) says pydantic.ValidationError 'continue[s] to propagate uncaught' and treats it as a schema bug. So a config that started fine before this diff now fails with a raw traceback out of asyncio.run, not the friendly logged exit used for TOML corruption (_log_corrupt_config_and_exit). The docstring says rejecting disabled instances is intended, so the rejection is the control working. The defect is the missing user-facing error path for what is now a user-config error and no longer a schema bug. Whether scheme-less URLs are a supported input is not established, so the compatibility question is left as needs_verification.
findings.title: Stricter URL validator turns previously-loadable configs into an uncaught startup traceback
findings.why_it_matters: After upgrading, a homelab user with a stale or scheme-less URL on a disabled instance gets a container crash-loop with a traceback and no guidance.

findings.problem: validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:150-171) checks BLOCKED_HOSTS by exact string match. It applies ipaddress.ip_address only to dotted literals. `http://metadata.google.internal./` gives hostname 'metadata.google.internal.' with a trailing dot, which is not in BLOCKED_HOSTS. `http://2852039166/` (169.254.169.254 written as a decimal integer) raises ValueError in ip_address(str) and falls into the 'arbitrary hostname' branch. Both pass the check, and at connect time the resolver or libc can map them to the metadata endpoint. The strict validate_arr_url equally allowed these inputs before this diff, so this is a pre-existing gap and stays under the cap. pending: confirm that httpx/getaddrinfo in the deployed image resolves the decimal-integer host form to 169.254.169.254.
findings.title: Metadata-host blocklist can be bypassed with a trailing-dot FQDN or a decimal/octal IPv4 form (pre-existing in the shared helper)
findings.why_it_matters: The control this diff adds to config load is meant to block cloud-metadata SSRF, and these forms get around it.

agent_notes: This diff overall is a security hardening change, not a regression: before it, InstanceConfig.url had zero SSRF validation at config-load time (any URL in triggarr.toml, including cloud-metadata addresses, loaded unchecked). The new field_validator closes that gap for metadata/link-local/unspecified/multicast targets while deliberately keeping loopback/localhost permitted for config-load only, per the project's own documented threat model (71-02-PLAN.md, D-01/D-02). I verified the web settings form (routes.py:561) still applies the strict validate_arr_url before any instance URL reaches this new, relaxed validator, so no new remotely-triggerable exposure was found; the one finding above is a low-confidence, forward-looking note about that design choice, not a defect in the diff as written.

findings.problem: The new validate_url_ssrf field_validator (via validate_arr_url_config) permits loopback IP literals (127.0.0.1, ::1) and the 'localhost' DNS name for URLs loaded from triggarr.toml, while link-local/unspecified/multicast IP literals and known cloud-metadata hosts are still blocked. This is a documented, deliberate relaxation (D-01/D-02, .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-02-PLAN.md) scoped to the config-load trust boundary (operator-edited TOML file), not the web settings form, which keeps the strict validate_arr_url (routes.py:561) that still rejects loopback IP literals before any InstanceConfig is constructed. I traced the only user-facing URL input path (the settings POST handler) and confirmed it calls the strict validator first, so this relaxation does not appear to open a new remotely-reachable SSRF surface today.
findings.title: Config-load SSRF validator intentionally permits loopback/localhost URLs
findings.why_it_matters: If any future code path ever constructs InstanceConfig/Settings directly from externally-influenced data (e.g. a config-import feature, an API endpoint, or a future refactor that removes the routes.py:561 pre-check) without first running the strict validate_arr_url, the relaxed variant would allow an attacker-supplied URL pointing at 127.0.0.1/localhost -- letting Triggarr's HTTP client reach internal-only services on its own host. Currently no such path exists in the reviewed code, so this is a forward-looking note rather than a demonstrated bypass.

agent_notes: Checked for an import cycle and found none. triggarr/web/validation.py imports only the standard library (ipaddress, re, urllib.parse) and nothing from triggarr, and triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty. So the new edge models/config -> web/validation is one-way, and loading the web package does not pull in routes or anything else that imports models.config.

Layer direction: this is the first time triggarr/models/ depends on triggarr/web/. Before this diff, models/config.py imported only pydantic, pydantic_settings and the standard library. The plan allows it explicitly. .planning/phases/71-presentation-rewrite/71-02-PLAN.md key_links says the link goes "to: triggarr.web.validation.validate_arr_url_config" "via: field_validator local import + call, raising ValueError". The diff matches that, so it is not a finding. If the team wants to remove the inversion later, validation.py is pure and has no web dependencies, so it could move to a neutral module (for example triggarr/validation.py or triggarr/models/validation.py) with web/validation.py re-exporting it. This is optional cleanup, not a defect.

The function-local import is not actually needed today. The plan says a module-level import 'would risk a circular import', but web.validation imports nothing from triggarr, so a top-level import would also work. The local import is harmless and is a reasonable guard if validation.py ever gains a triggarr import. The codebase already does function-local cross-layer imports in triggarr/search/scheduler.py:532 and :538 (from triggarr.web.routes) and triggarr/state.py:24 and :32, so the style fits.

Pattern consistency: the validator follows the existing InstanceConfig.url field_validator style (classmethod that raises ValueError so Pydantic turns it into a ValidationError) and the existing (ok, err) tuple contract of the web/validation helpers. I found no deviation.

Duplication, below the rule of three: validate_arr_url_config (web/validation.py:111) almost duplicates validate_arr_url (web/validation.py:56), differing only in whether loopback is allowed. That is two copies, it was added in the earlier commit 14eecb5 rather than this diff, and the plan asks for it as a 'sibling function'. Not a finding. If a third variant appears, merge them into one function with an allow_loopback parameter.

Behavior across modules (for the impact/bugs agents): the settings-save path in triggarr/web/routes.py:561 still calls the strict validate_arr_url, which blocks loopback, while config load now uses the relaxed variant. So a loopback URL can load from triggarr.toml but be rejected if re-saved through the web form, unless routes.py was changed elsewhere in phase 71. Plan line 256 suggests the form path is meant to accept loopback too. pending: confirm whether 71-02 or a later plan switches routes.py:561 to the relaxed validator. This is a correctness and consistency question, not an architecture finding.

agent_notes: Blast radius: InstanceConfig is the per-instance model for radarr, sonarr and lidarr, held in Settings dicts (triggarr/models/config.py:177-179). Every Settings construction now runs the validator. That covers startup load_settings (triggarr/config.py:227 via ensure_config at :371), the settings POST (triggarr/web/routes.py:597), add-instance (routes.py:790, empty URL, passes) and the post-auth reloads (routes.py:1199/1462/1511/1535). The reloads re-read TOML written from already-validated settings, so they cannot newly fail unless someone edits the file while the app is running.

Settings form: routes.py:561 already applies the stricter validate_arr_url, which also blocks loopback, before SettingsModel(**new_config). Anything the new relaxed validator rejects was already rejected earlier on that path, so the web UI behaves the same. The only path with new behaviour is a hand-edited TOML loaded at startup.

The relaxed validator differs from the strict one only by allowing loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1, ::ffff:127.x). That keeps same-host installs with loopback literals working at startup. A pre-existing inconsistency remains and is not introduced here: a TOML with http://127.0.0.1 loads fine, but any later settings-form save is rejected by the strict validator at routes.py:561.
No public API signatures changed, and there are no DB, schema or migration effects: detect_and_migrate_v22 rewrites TOML without new constraints, and URL values are not persisted elsewhere.

Performance: negligible. The check is a urlparse plus an ipaddress parse per instance at load time. After the first call, the function-local import is a sys.modules dict lookup. No DNS resolution happens.

Import layering: models.config now depends on triggarr.web.validation at call time. triggarr/web/__init__.py is empty and validation.py imports only stdlib, so there is no circular-import risk today. Still, a model-layer module now reaches into the web package, which is an architecture smell rather than a defect.

Fixtures: test and README URLs are all http hostnames (http://radarr:7878 and similar), which pass the new check. I could not run the test suite because the review-agent hook allows read-only commands only.

Verdict: this is a tightening change, and I found no demonstrated regression for any URL form the project supports. It is shippable as-is. Optional follow-up: a friendly startup error instead of a raw ValidationError traceback.

findings.fix_hint: Optionally catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and log a friendly 'invalid URL for <app>/<instance>' message before sys.exit(1), matching the corrupt-TOML path.
findings.problem: validate_url_ssrf runs every time InstanceConfig is built, including through load_settings (triggarr/config.py:227) from ensure_config at startup (triggarr/config.py:371). The docstring at triggarr/config.py:345 says pydantic.ValidationError is not caught there, so it propagates as a raw traceback. Some TOML URLs that loaded before now fail validation at triggarr/web/validation.py:143-166: non-http(s) schemes, `http://0.0.0.0:7878`, link-local literals such as `http://169.254.10.5`, `http://[fe80::1%eth0]`, multicast literals, and IPv4-mapped CGNAT literals such as `http://[::ffff:100.64.1.2]`. A disabled instance is also checked, which the docstring says is intended. In a Docker deployment with a restart policy, the container then restart-loops with a traceback instead of the friendly message used for corrupt TOML (_log_corrupt_config_and_exit). This is under the cap because none of these values is in the supported input contract. The README documents only http hostname URLs (README.md:151-179), and the settings form has always rejected all of them through the stricter validate_arr_url (triggarr/web/routes.py:561). Rejecting them is the control working. pending: a documented or persisted deployment that relies on one of these URL forms, e.g. 0.0.0.0 used as a same-host alias, would turn this into a real regression.
findings.title: New load-time URL check can stop Triggarr from starting when a hand-edited TOML URL was accepted before
findings.why_it_matters: Upgrading users whose configs fall outside the documented contract get a crash loop with no clear explanation, rather than a clear error message.

findings.fix_hint: Normalize the hostname (strip the trailing dot, and parse numeric-only or octal forms via socket.inet_aton) before the BLOCKED_HOSTS and ip_address checks, in both validators.
findings.problem: validate_arr_url_config blocks metadata endpoints by exact hostname match against BLOCKED_HOSTS (triggarr/web/validation.py:150) and by ipaddress.ip_address parsing (validation.py:154). Three kinds of value get through. Decimal or octal IPv4 forms such as `http://2852039166/` and `http://0251.0376.0251.0376/` make ip_address() raise ValueError, which validation.py:167-171 treats as a hostname, yet the OS resolver may still map them to 169.254.169.254. A trailing-dot FQDN such as `http://metadata.google.internal./` also misses the exact-match set. The strict validate_arr_url (validation.py:85-100) has the same gaps and the pre-change load path had no check at all, so this diff adds no new exposure. It is a pre-existing gap and does not weaken the new control. pending: confirm whether httpx/getaddrinfo in the deployed image resolves decimal/octal hosts to the metadata IP.
findings.title: Pre-existing gap: non-canonical IP encodings and FQDN trailing dot get past the metadata/link-local block (SSRF)
findings.why_it_matters: These are the remaining ways around the metadata-IP block that this diff sets out to enforce.

findings.fix_hint: Catch ValidationError in ensure_config and log only loc/msg with errors(include_input=False).
findings.problem: When a field validator raises ValueError, Pydantic's ValidationError text includes `input_value=<url>`. At startup the error is not caught (triggarr/config.py:345), so the traceback goes to stderr or Docker logs directly rather than through the Loguru redacting sink. A rejected URL that carries userinfo, such as `ftp://user:secret@radarr:7878` or `http://user:pw@0.0.0.0:7878`, would print the credential. The same pattern already exists in reject_apikey_in_url (config.py:65-86); this diff only adds new kinds of rejection that reach it. pending: show that a supported config is likely to put credentials in URL userinfo.
findings.title: Rejected URL is printed verbatim in the startup traceback and skips the redacting log sink (credential exposure)
findings.why_it_matters: This project's convention is that secrets never reach logs; an uncaught startup traceback is an unredacted channel.
